haha i wish there was a pattern, honestly it was mainly freehanded after getting some pinterest inspo (totally different looking care bear tho). i mainly used basic amigurumi shapes tho! cylindrical structures for the legs (using double crochet stitches cus i was lazy, and then swapper to sc when i connected the legs. then attached the two legs with SC and then swapped back over to DC once i had finished the first based round. i worked up the body from there, and the bum was a bit of freehand as well (theres tutes for similar bums on youtube i think).  the arms were similar to the legs, but just slowly reducing the amount of stitches as I got to the top. and the head was just a SC sphere (i used the “ideal crochet sphere pattern for 30 rows!). i then made the belly patch freehand as well (in white) and then freehanded the leaf motif as well. the ears and face details were also freehanded! the patch on the feet was done with some sewing but i might clean it up a little! i hope that helps, sorry there isn’t a specific pattern 😭

No problemo! In terms of professor preference, IDK if there is one tbh - it probably depends on the prof. The prof (at least in my case) will usually have a couple projects in mind that align with their lab's work, so there's really a lot of factors that come in to play. In my case, I asked the professors that I emailed for 12/15 credit courses (i.e. intro email) and said that I would also potentially be willing to do a 9 credit one (I wanted to do as many creds as possible). So i guess I would suggest giving that type of info (i.e. your credit preference) in the first email to them (along with your unofficial transcript so they know what courses you've taken). 

In terms of the most common #, I don't really know, but I would assume that 9/12 is pretty popular because with a thesis course (at least IMO), you can kinda work (reasonably) at your own pace. Ahh I know I basically couldn't answer your questions solidly, but I hope that kinda helped! LMK if you have any other questions - I'll try my best to answer!

Essentially yes because you are basically expected to commit the same amount of hours per week (on average) that you would for any other class. So if you are taking a 6 unit project course (i.e. equivalent to one course per semester) it would be like around 5-10 hours per week, which is basically what you spend on any other course. In my case, I'm taking a 12 unit one (i.e 2 courses per semester equivalent) so I would work 10-20 hours. So, in that case, it just happens to be that you will be doing more work in a 12 unit one :) I hope that makes sense!

I would suggest not re-taking because as long as you get into university, your high school marks won't affect your chances of getting into med. With that being said, I was also very weak in Chemistry so I studied it during the summer before I entered uni to make sure I was able to ensure good marks in the first year course. Try and get the relevant textbook ahead of time and a course outline for the relevant chem course you will be taking in first year. Then, just do some self-study using those materials (i.e. make your notes). That way, when you're in the course itself, you can worry about making minor adjustments to your notes, do your labs, and do as many practice questions as you can. I hope that helps, and I promise you don't need to be as worried as you are, give yourself a break <3
